content.when_required: Investor has SIGNIFICANT INFLUENCE over investee (presumed at 20-50% ownership, but evaluate other factors)

ownership_levels.less_than_20_percent: Presumed NO significant influence → Fair value method (ASC 321) unless evidence of influence
ownership_levels.20_to_50_percent: Presumed significant influence → Equity method (unless evidence rebuts)
ownership_levels.over_50_percent: Control → Consolidation required (equity method not used in consolidated statements)

equity_method_adjustments.investee_reports_income: DR Investment, CR Equity in Investee Income (investor's share of investee's net income)
equity_method_adjustments.investee_declares_dividends: DR Cash (or Dividends Receivable), CR Investment (dividends reduce investment, not income)
equity_method_adjustments.formula: Investment balance = Cost + Share of income - Dividends received - Amortization of basis difference

basis_difference.definition: Excess of cost over book value of net assets acquired (or vice versa)
basis_difference.allocation: Allocate to: (1) Undervalued/overvalued identifiable assets (amortize), (2) Goodwill (no amortization)
basis_difference.amortization: Amortize basis difference assigned to depreciable/amortizable assets. Reduce equity in income.
basis_difference.example: Purchase 30% for $150K. BV of net assets 30% × $400K = $120K. Basis difference $30K. If $20K to equipment (10-year life), amortize $2K/year. If $10K to goodwill, no amortization.

content.one_line_consolidation: Equity method called 'one-line consolidation' because investor's share of investee's net income reported as single line item (Equity in Investee Income)

year_1.facts: Jan 1: Purchase 30% of investee for $200K. Investee BV of net assets $600K (30% = $180K). Basis difference $20K attributed to equipment (10-year life). Investee reports NI $100K, pays dividends $40K.
entries: Income: DR Investment $28K, CR Equity in Investee Income $28K

content.investee_reports_oci: Investor recognizes share of investee's OCI. DR Investment, CR OCI.

investee_reports_loss.recognition: Recognize share of loss: DR Equity in Investee Loss, CR Investment
investee_reports_loss.zero_balance_rule: Reduce investment to zero, then stop (unless investor has guaranteed obligations or committed to provide support)
investee_reports_loss.subsequent_income: If investee subsequently profitable, first recover suspended losses before recognizing income

impairment.when_test: When indicators of impairment (other than temporary decline)
impairment.test: If FV < carrying amount and decline is other-than-temporary, recognize impairment loss

sale_of_investment.entry: DR Cash (proceeds), CR Investment (carrying amount), CR/DR Gain or Loss (plug)

intercompany_transactions.upstream_sale: Investee sells to investor. Defer investor's share of profit until realized.
intercompany_transactions.downstream_sale: Investor sells to investee. Defer 100% of profit until realized (investor controls transaction).
intercompany_transactions.example: Investor owns 40%. Investee sells inventory (cost $60K) to investor for $100K. Investor resells for $120K. Investor's share of unrealized profit: 40% × $40K = $16K. Defer $16K equity income until inventory sold to third party.

cpa_exam_tips: Investment increases by share of income, decreases by dividends received
Amortize basis difference on depreciable assets (reduces equity income)
Goodwill in basis difference NOT amortized
Equity income = Share of NI - Amortization of basis difference
Defer unrealized profit on intercompany transactions

basis_difference_allocation: 2. Allocate to specific identifiable assets (FV - BV)
4. Amortize identifiable assets over useful life
common_mistakes: Recording dividends as income (should reduce investment)
Forgetting to amortize basis difference (reduces equity income)
Using equity method when >50% ownership (should consolidate instead)

key_points: Investment increases by share of income, decreases by dividends
Equity income = Share of NI - Amortization of basis difference
Basis difference: Allocate to identifiable assets (amortize) and goodwill (no amortization)
Defer unrealized profit on intercompany transactions
Investment balance = Cost + Income - Dividends - Amortization +/- OCI
